title: Agents, Access, and the Future of Machine Identity — Nick Nisi (WorkOS) + Lizzie Siegle (Cloudflare)
talk_summary: A WorkOS + Cloudflare developer-advocate talk demoing an MCP server deployed on Cloudflare Workers with OAuth (WorkOS) so an agent acts on a user's behalf, storing per-user state in Durable Objects and orders in KV. The substantive content is machine identity/authorization for agents, not agent orchestration efficiency.

takeaways.technique: OAuth-scoped agent identity per acting user
takeaways.what_they_do: The MCP server requires an OAuth sign-in so the agent's tools execute with a JWT identifying who it acts for (name, email, roles/permissions), rather than a shared static token.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we need like the same kind of credentials and uh authorization that we do with userf facing projects. We need the agents to do that as well

takeaways.technique: Audit trail on agent tool calls
takeaways.what_they_do: They argue OAuth tooling should record on whose behalf an action ran, why, and where it failed, so agent actions are traceable.
takeaways.evidence_quote: especially the audit trail as well ... we can see why this interacted this way on whose behalf was it on and what was the end result where did it fail

takeaways.what_they_do: Durable Objects are spun up per user so stored context (e.g., a 'demo mode' flag) is unique per user and close to them for fast retrieval.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You can spin them up per user ... that's in unique for every user of it

takeaways.technique: Wrap existing APIs as MCP tools with auth
takeaways.what_they_do: They expose a simple existing flow (order a shirt) as an MCP tool so the agent reuses the same API humans use, gated by OAuth.
takeaways.evidence_quote: MCP is effectively just an API. Uh so we're just like you know getting it caught up with the tools that we already have
